# Technical document: ball possession (More than a Hack 2027, Phase 1)

**Team:** DeculGirl  
**Repository:** [https://github.com/yonakatitin/more-than-a-hack-2027](https://github.com/yonakatitin/more-than-a-hack-2027)  
**Submitted file:** `v4.csv`, generated by `python -m src.pipeline v4` (written to `evaluation/results/`, which is git-ignored by design) and uploaded as `DeculGirl.csv`  
**Environment:** Python 3.10.7, numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3 (`requirements.txt` pins numpy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.1.0)

## 1. Summary

A transparent, rule-based pipeline with no learned model and no training. It labels every video frame of the tactical recording `H`, `A`, `D` or `X` using only the automatic tracking and the set-piece windows of Smart Tagging. Every parameter is a stated football or physics assumption, not a value fitted to this match, with one exception that section 7 states (the 18-frame confirmation time). We chose rules over a model because the competition forbids tuning on the match's ground truth and we used no external labelled data, so a learned model had nothing legitimate to learn from.

## 2. Approach

Three layers, then an assembly step.

1. **Control.** On a frame with a tracked ball, the nearest tracked player controls it if he is within 2.5 m. Otherwise nobody does (loose, in the air, or untracked ball). 
2. **Confirmation and hold.** A change of possession is accepted only after the new team has controlled the ball for 18 frames (0.72 s at 25 FPS), with gaps between observations of up to 18 frames. The change is dated back to the first of those observations, so confirming adds no delay. While nobody controls the ball the last team keeps it, as the challenge rules state for loose balls. This removes the frame-level flicker of "nearest player wins": the same idea as the provided smoothing baselines, but event-based instead of a fixed window. 
3. **Dead ball** (`D`) from these sources: 
   - A `SET PIECES` window from Smart Tagging (kick offs excluded) starts a dead-ball stretch. It ends when the median speed of the tracked players (smoothed over 1 s) stays above 1.5 m/s for 3 s, and lasts at most 20 s. 
   - Any of five tracking-only layers, restricted to graded frames, with gaps of up to 1 s bridged and runs shorter than 2 s dropped (this cleaning applies to these five layers together, not to the set-piece windows). They catch stoppages that Smart Tagging does not mark (fouls, injuries, VAR); Smart Tagging lists only 5 free kicks in the whole match, so many such stoppages are untagged: 
     - the ball outside the pitch for at least 1 s; 
     - the ball inside a 1 m circle for 1 s and the median player speed under 1.0 m/s; 
     - the median player speed under 0.5 m/s for 10 s, ball seen or not (long stoppages); 
     - players clustered (RMS distance from their centroid under 16 m) and slower than 1.0 m/s for 5 s; 
     - frames 110,808-113,741: graded, and all `D`, as published in the organisers' FAQ. 
4. **Assembly.** Possession is computed separately inside each stretch of live play, so it never carries across a stoppage: the first team to control the ball after a restart owns the frames before it (look-ahead, since processing is offline). A live stretch with no observed control at all takes the nearest known team. Frames outside the two halves are `X`. 

Result on the 158,857 graded frames: 70,060 `H`, 59,905 `A`, 28,892 `D`, 217 and 228 label runs per half.

## 3. Assets

- **Used:** tactical tracking (ATD): positions of the track slots and of the ball, and the team of each slot. Smart Tagging: the SET PIECES windows. The two kick-off frames come from a constant in the provided starter code (starter/load_smart_tagging.py). The five tracking-only dead-ball layers come from the pipeline of a team member (DyangPB/mtah-DeculGirl-submission) and are re-implemented in `src/deadball_extra.py`. 
- **Examined and dropped:**
  - Smart Tagging `Team` tags and phase codes. `DATA.md` says some are `N/A` (every throw-in), and we could not confirm what the tag means in the defending phases without relying on the ground truth, so we did not use it. We later measured it against our own control rule (never the ground truth): it names the team the phase is about, so in a defending phase the team with the ball is the opponent (`DEFENDING IN ATTACKING THIRD`: the tagged team has the ball 16% of the time) and in the attacking phases it is the tagged team (56-84%). We still do not use it in v4. 
  - "Ball outside the pitch" as a dead-ball signal on its own: it adds only about 0.5% of graded frames beyond what set-piece windows already cover. v4 keeps it as one of the five layers. 
  - A switching-cost decoder with a small players-only model for the stretches where the ball is not tracked, and weak evidence from the nearest team of a loose ball. In a test that hides the ball where it is tracked, accuracy on the hidden frames rose from 0.615 to about 0.73, but none of these variants scored better on the public window, and none was adopted. 
  - The ball standing still for several seconds as a dead-ball signal beyond the layers above: it adds only about 1% of graded frames. 
- **Not used:** the video, the broadcast recording (not synchronised), and the homography.

## 4. Training data

None. No labelled dataset was used and nothing was trained, tuned or calibrated on the provided game, its ground truth or its video.

## 5. Possession rules implemented

- Controlled possession needs a player within 2.5 m. Passing close to the ball is not enough (hence the 0.72 s confirmation). 
- Loose, contested or untracked ball: possession stays with the last team that controlled it. 
- Restart: ownership is not carried over a stoppage. The first team to control the ball owns it. 
- Dead ball: tagged set pieces, the five tracking-only layers of section 2, and the period before the second-half kick off. Dead-ball ownership is not asked for, so `D` carries no team.

## 6. Parameters and where they come from

All values are fixed assumptions, chosen on football or physics grounds and not optimised against any score, except the confirmation time (see section 7).

| Parameter | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Control distance | 2.5 m | A player can only play the ball from within a couple of metres; tracking error is about 1 m |
| Confirmation time | 18 frames (0.72 s) | A sustained control interval of approximately 0.72 seconds, long enough to suppress tracking flicker while detecting genuine possession changes more quickly. |
| Gap tolerance while confirming | 18 frames (0.72 s) | Brief tracking drop-outs should not reset the count |
| Resume speed / hold | 1.5 m/s / 3 s | Slightly above relaxed walking (about 1.3-1.4 m/s), sustained rather than a spike |
| Maximum dead stretch per set piece | 20 s | A restart rarely takes longer; also bounds the damage if speed never rises |
| Ball outside the pitch | 1 s | Not a tracking flicker |
| Quiet team threshold / duration | 0.5 m/s / 10 s | Far below walking speed, for long enough to be a stoppage |
| Huddle | RMS distance under 16 m, median speed under 1.0 m/s, 5 s | Clustered tail of the team shape (bottom ~4%); slower than normal play |
| Shortest dead run / bridged gap | 2 s / 1 s | A throw-in lasts 5-8 s; shorter gaps are tracking drop-outs |
| Speed smoothing / jump limit | 1 s / 12 m/s | Reduces noise; faster than a sprint is a tracking jump |

Transparency note: the speed values around set pieces, and the team-shape distribution used for the clustering threshold, were inspected on the provided tracking (descriptive statistics only, no ground truth) before adopting the thresholds above.

## 7. Use of the public ground truth

The 5-minute public file was used to check that the pipeline runs end to end and, during exploration, to read what labels look like (label shares, ball visibility). We also compared Smart Tagging team tags against it to understand them, and did not use the result.

**Version v4 was not built blind to its score.** The 18-frame confirmation comes from the v3 experiment, chosen after the public score of v2 (0.4457) was known. The combination of the v3 possession rule with the fuller dead-ball detection was picked after the public scores of several variants had been seen: a tracking-only pipeline 0.3758, the same with set-piece windows 0.4457, v3 0.4649, and this combination 0.4757. Other variants (a switching-cost decoder with a players-only model, a Smart Tagging phase prior, extra evidence for loose balls) were also scored on that window and none was adopted; their spellF1 ranged from 0.39 to 0.44.

Public check (17 possessions, too few to rank on): spellF1 0.4757, macroF1 0.6764.

Per-class breakdown on the same window: H F1 0.794, A F1 0.782, D F1 0.453 (precision 0.76, recall 0.32). The scorer's own bootstrap states that gaps below about 0.33 in spellF1 are inside the noise with 17 possessions, so these numbers show that the pipeline works, not that it is better than another version. The gain in macroF1 over v3 (0.6466 to 0.6764) comes from dead-ball recall rising from 0.25 to 0.32.

## 8. Checks on the submitted file

These checks do not need the answer key. They were computed independently from the uploaded file, over both graded halves (158,857 frames).

| Check | baseline_smooth50 | v4 |
|---|---|---|
| File passes validate_submission.py | yes | yes (199,319 rows, frames 0 to 199,318) |
| H / A possessions | 594 | 353 |
| Possessions shorter than 19 frames | 98 | 4 |
| Median possession length | 4.6 s | 9.9 s |
| D runs / median length | 133 / 7.6 s | 92 / 7.8 s |
| Label runs per half |  | 217 and 228 |
| X inside the graded frames | 0 | 0 |

19 frames (0.76 s) is the shortest real possession in the public ground truth, so a count of possessions below it is a measure of flicker. v4 differs from baseline_smooth50 on 66,029 of the 158,857 graded frames (41.6%). The Barcelona share of live frames is 53.9% (70,060 of 129,965), which matches the figure in the limitations below.

## 9. Limitations

- **Long missing-ball stretches.** The ball is untracked on about 41% of graded frames, often for tens of seconds. There the pipeline only holds the last team and has no model of play from the players alone. Over a gap longer than 5 s between two observations of control (59% of graded frames lie in such gaps) the team changes in 36-47% of the cases, so holding the last team is close to a coin flip. This is the largest weakness. It cannot be measured on the public 5 minutes, where the ball is nearly always visible. 
- **Possible bias in missing-ball stretches.** Against the organisers' reference baseline (nearest player plus a +/-2 s vote, which only uses frames with a visible ball), the v2 labels leaned towards the away team in the long stretches where that baseline had no usable ball (about 62% away among live labels), which lowered v2's overall Barcelona share to 51%. In v4 the share is 53.9%. This was a descriptive comparison only and was not used to change the solution. We could not tell whether it reflects the real play or a bias of the hold-last rule. 
- **Dead ball is incomplete.** It covers tagged set pieces and the five tracking-only layers. Stoppages that are none of these (short fouls, parts of celebrations) are missed or only partly covered. On the public window, dead-ball recall is 0.32 (precision 0.76): about two thirds of the true dead-ball frames are labelled as play. A false dead ball cuts a real possession. 
- **Frozen tracker vs real stoppage.** The quiet and still layers cannot tell them apart without the video. 
- **Confirmation time.** The 18 frames were chosen after seeing a public score (section 7). A shorter confirmation catches quicker changes but raises the risk of false switches and fragmentation. 
- **Pre-kick-off block.** All frames from the start of the second graded half (frame 110,808) until its kick off (frame 113,742) are labelled dead ball. This is not an assumption of ours: the organisers' FAQ states that these 2,934 graded frames are all `D`. The first half is graded from the kick off itself, so it has no such block. 
- **First observation after a restart is trusted immediately,** so a stray frame can mislabel the first moments of a stretch. 
- **Thresholds are unverified.** They were not checked on external data.

## 10. With more time

Check the thresholds on an external dataset with tracking and events (license permitting), model the missing-ball periods from team shape and movement, replace the hold-last rule by a decoder with an explicit switching cost, and confirm the meaning of the Smart Tagging team tag with the organisers before using it. We tried a decoder of this kind and measured the meaning of the tag against our own control rule (section 3); the decoder improved a hide-the-ball test but not the public score, so it was not adopted, and the public window cannot show its effect.

## 11. Reproduction

The pipeline is deterministic: no randomness is used.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1          # Windows PowerShell
pip install -r requirements.txt
# unpack the data bundle into ./data (or set MTAH_DATA_DIR)
python -m src.pipeline v4            # writes evaluation/results/v4.csv
python evaluation/validate_submission.py evaluation/results/v4.csv
```

The first run parses the tracking file (about 1-2 minutes) and caches it in `data/cache`. Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt` (numpy 2.5.4, pandas 3.1.0); the v4 file was generated with Python 3.10.7, numpy 2.2.6 and pandas 2.3.3. Only `src/` is needed to reproduce the file; `analysis/` holds exploration scripts that print descriptive statistics, and `docs/changes_v4.md` describes the changes of v4. Rebuilding from scratch, after deleting the cache, gave a byte-identical file. The SHA-256 of the submitted file, generated on Windows (CRLF line endings), is `1983a2e5635e8d04ff77ec8468f9d9b508c2147c2696a7754c08c11b8ff43954`. On Linux or macOS the line endings, and therefore the hash, differ, so compare the labels rather than the hash.

## 12. Supplementary

A web review of the match tracking, with an unscored view of the labelled file, is at [https://mtah-deculgirl.shadypb.workers.dev/](https://mtah-deculgirl.shadypb.workers.dev/). It is supplementary; the submitted file is DeculGirl.csv, generated as described in section 11, and the site offers the same labels as DeculGirl_v4.csv.
